title: Rigveda 3.12: To Indra and Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.12: To Indra and Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.12 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Indra and Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 197r-197v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.12.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 197r
translation.original_text:
1indrā̍gnī̱ ā ga̍taṁ su̱taṁ gī̱rbhir nabho̱ vare̍ṇyam | a̱sya pā̍taṁ dhi̱yeṣi̱tā ||
2indrā̍gnī jari̱tuḥ sacā̍ ya̱jño ji̍gāti̱ ceta̍naḥ | a̱yā pā̍tam i̱maṁ su̱tam ||
3indra̍m a̱gniṁ ka̍vi̱cchadā̍ ya̱jñasya̍ jū̱tyā vṛ̍ṇe | tā soma̍sye̱ha tṛ̍mpatām ||
4to̱śā vṛ̍tra̱haṇā̍ huve sa̱jitvā̱nāpa̍rājitā | i̱ndrā̱gnī vā̍ja̱sāta̍mā ||
translation.text:
1MOVED, Indra-Agni, by our hymn, come to the juice, the precious dew: Dr.ink ye thereof, impelled by song.
2O Indra-Agni, with the man who lauds you comes the wakening rite: So drink ye both this juice assured.
3Through force of sacrifice I choose Indra-Agni who love the wise: With Soma let these sate them here.
4Indra and Agni I invoke, joint-victors, bounteous, unsubdued, Foe-slayers, best to win the spoil.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 197r (numbered 7r by the scribe) (OPenn image 198, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.11.7 ‹prayāṃsi vāhasā dāśvān aśnoti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 197v (numbered 7v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.12.5 ‹-nītha-vidaḥ jaritāraḥ indrāgnī iti›. Verses 3.12.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1indrāgnī iti | ā | gatam | sutam | gīḥ-bhiḥ | nabhaḥ | vareṇyam | asya | pātam | dhiyā | iṣitā
2indrāgnī iti | jarituḥ | sacā | yajñaḥ | jigāti | cetanaḥ | ayā | pātam | imam | sutam
3indram | agnim | kavi-chadā | yajñasya | jūtyā | vṛṇe | tā | somasya | iha | tṛmpatām
4tośā | vṛtra-hanā | huve | sa-jityvānā | aparājitā | indrāgnī iti | vāja-sātamā

translation.original_ref: RV 3.12.5-9 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 197v
translation.original_text:
5pra vā̍m arcanty u̱kthino̍ nīthā̱vido̍ jari̱tāra̍ḥ | indrā̍gnī̱ iṣa̱ ā vṛ̍ṇe ||
6indrā̍gnī nava̱tim puro̍ dā̱sapa̍tnīr adhūnutam | sā̱kam eke̍na̱ karma̍ṇā ||
7indrā̍gnī̱ apa̍sa̱s pary upa̱ pra ya̍nti dhī̱taya̍ḥ | ṛ̱tasya̍ pa̱thyā̱3̱̍ anu̍ ||
8indrā̍gnī tavi̱ṣāṇi̍ vāṁ sa̱dhasthā̍ni̱ prayā̍ṁsi ca | yu̱vor a̱ptūrya̍ṁ hi̱tam ||
9indrā̍gnī roca̱nā di̱vaḥ pari̱ vāje̍ṣu bhūṣathaḥ | tad vā̍ṁ ceti̱ pra vī̱rya̍m ||
translation.text:
5Indra and Agni, singers skilled in melody hymn you, bringing lauds: I choose you for the sacred food.
6Indra and Agni, ye cast down the ninety forts which Dâsas held, Together, with one mighty deed.
7To Indra-Agni reverent thoughts go forward from the holy task Along the path of sacred Law.
8O Indra-Agni, powers are yours, and dwellings and delightful food Good is your readiness to act.
9Indra and Agni, in your deeds of might ye deck heaven's lucid realms: Famed is that hero strength of yours.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 197v (numbered 7v by the scribe) (OPenn image 199, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.12.5 ‹-nītha-vidaḥ jaritāraḥ indrāgnī iti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 198r (numbered 8r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.13.2 ‹-saniṣyantaḥ avase›. Verses 3.12.5-9 end on this page; 3.12.5 begins on fol. 197r (numbered 7r by the scribe).

6indrāgnī iti | navatim | puraḥ | dāsa-patnīḥ | adhūnutam | sākam | ekena | karmaṇā
7indrāgnī iti | apasaḥ | pari | upa | pra | yanti | dhītayaḥ | ṛtasya | pathyāḥ | anu
8indrāgnī iti | taviṣāṇi | vām | sadha-sthāni | prayāṃsi | ca | yuvoḥ | ap-tūryam | hitam
